newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products end lower on fund selling, wheat.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products end lower on fund selling, wheat.

text.p: A late tumble in wheat futures and fund selling pressed CBOT soy product futures to a lower close, traders said.
Refco Inc sold 1,000 lots of December soymeal which pressured that month on spreads with the deferred contracts, they said.
But the market was underpinned by the Census Bureau's October crush report which showed soyoil stocks at a level below expectations.
"Oil stocks below two billion lbs was a little supportive for oil," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
The Census Bureau's October crush data showed U.S. soyoil stocks at the end of October at 1.991 billion lbs. The market had expected the stocks to total at least two billion.

Soymeal also was influenced by adjustment of the spread because December had been climbing to a strong premium to the other contracts recently. Soymeal stocks seen in the October crush report were at 184,106 tons, below September's 188,293 tons and above the 167,654 tons a year ago.
Soyoil closed unchanged to 0.14 cent per lb lower, with December down 0.08 at 23.29. Soymeal was $1.80 per ton lower to $1.00 higher, with December down $1.80 at $238.20.
Soyoil futures volume was estimated at 15,000 contracts, below the 15,169 traded Wednesday, according to the CBOT. Soymeal volume was estimated at 28,000 contracts, below the 31,945 traded Wednesday.
